svg.title: The actual specialization unit for singular product coefficients
svg.desc: A product over an arbitrary parameter scheme has local fibre P. Its restriction map factors through the constant field unit and the singular coefficient tensor comparison. Both stalk maps are isomorphisms. Exact sheaf filtrations extend the result to finite prime powers without a flatness assumption.
svg.text: Singular coefficients in a fixed product
k algebraically closed; ℓ invertible in k.
X/k separated of finite type; E bounded constructible.
1. Every geometric local test
Y = X ×ₖ B

S = B₍b̄₎; choose any geometric point t̄ → S.
P = Y₍ȳ₎ ×ₛ t̄
P is the strict-local fibre used in the ULA test.
B is arbitrary. The point t̄ need not come from a trait.
2. The restriction is the adjunction unit
For g : t̄ → S, the constant-section unit gives
Fℓ → (Rg* Fℓ)₍b̄₎ = Fℓ[0].

tensor comparison β ≅
RΓ(P, E|ₚ)
3. Finite prime powers, including nonflat stalks
Filter a sheaf M by ℓʳM. Each successive quotient
is killed by ℓ, so its local test is already proved.
Exact sequences give the test for M.
Ordinary truncation triangles give it for bounded E.
The proof uses these finite triangles at every base change.
No derived reduction modulo ℓ is used.
Proofs: L.5.1.1, L.6.1.1–L.6.2.1. Geometry is schematic.
